Abbreviate

uh-BREV-ee-ate — rhymes with ate, stress on second syllable · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To abbreviate something is to shorten it, usually by cutting out part of it while keeping it recognizable.

Doctors abbreviate 'blood pressure' to 'BP' in their notes.

Worked Example

A student writing a lab report abbreviates 'sodium chloride' to 'NaCl' so readers still know exactly what she means.

Abbreviate is the precise word here because the student is shortening something while keeping it fully recognizable to the audience. Simply saying 'shorten' wouldn't capture that key detail — you could shorten a word in ways that make it hard to recognize.

How Abbreviate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

shorten

shorten: to make something less long

condense

condense: to pack the same content into less space

truncate

truncate: to cut something off abruptly at the end

Antonyms

expand

expand: to make larger or more detailed

lengthen

lengthen: to make something longer or draw it out

How Strong Is It? — condense → shorten → abbreviate → truncate

condense vs. abbreviate

condense vs. abbreviate: Condense is gentler than abbreviate: to condense is to squeeze the same content into less space, while to abbreviate is to actually cut something down to a shorter form.

shorten vs. abbreviate

shorten vs. abbreviate: Shorten is the general, milder term next to abbreviate: shorten means to reduce length in any way, while abbreviate specifically trims something down while keeping it recognizable.

truncate vs. abbreviate

truncate vs. abbreviate: Truncate is harsher than abbreviate: to abbreviate is to shorten something carefully so it stays recognizable, while to truncate is to chop off its end abruptly.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ab-

Prefix — ab-: to, toward (an assimilated form of Latin ad-)

Root — brevi

Root — brevi: short (from Latin brevis, 'short')

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ab- ('to,' an assimilated form of Latin ad-) + brevi ('short,' from Latin brevis) + -ate ('make') builds 'to make short' — to abbreviate something is to shorten it, usually by cutting out part of it while keeping it recognizable.

Use the root in a new word: brief

Use the root in a new word: brief: Keep your answer brief — brief comes from Latin brevis, 'short,' the same root that lets you abbreviate a long phrase into a few letters.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Use abbreviate when you shorten something while keeping it recognizable — especially for technical terms, long phrases, or official writing. For casual shortening with no special focus on recognizability, the plain word 'shorten' is simpler and more direct.
